subject: creating a cohort of patients as copy of another cohort with clone function

messages.author: ab5036ff14cc0b00
messages.subject: creating a cohort of patients as copy of another cohort with clone function
parts:
Hello,

I need to create two groups of patients (arrivals) with identical attributes (age, sex, time with disease, previous treatments and other characteristics).
My approach is to generate an arrival and then use "clone" to create a copy of the arrival with an exact copy of the attributes, then each patient (arrival) follows a different path of treatment with different overall survival within the model.
I have found two issues:
  1. The main one: I don't know how to identify the original and the clone in the final results (monitor).  So far I only see two Arrivals0 (Patient0, Patient0) but for a large analysis of the table provided by the monitor I don't find a flag to identify original and clone.
  2. So far I haven't been successful in creating an exact copy of each arrival and its attributes.  Some attributes are not being copied with the same value to the clone
As you can see I am not using Synchronize as I don't want to get original and clone back together as they end up with different results through the model.

Thanks for your help,

Pablo.

> My approach is to generate an arrival and then use "clone" to create a copy of the arrival with an exact copy of the attributes, then each patient (arrival) follows a different path of treatment with different overall survival within the model.
> I have found two issues:
>
> The main one: I don't know how to identify the original and the clone in the final results (monitor). So far I only see two Arrivals0 (Patient0, Patient0) but for a large analysis of the table provided by the monitor I don't find a flag to identify original and clone.
> So far I haven't been successful in creating an exact copy of each arrival and its attributes. Some attributes are not being copied with the same value to the clone

Short answer: don't use clone() for this. Its main use case is for
parallel tasks in which you see the same arrival doing multiple
things. If you want the two groups of arrivals to be distinguishable,
then set up two generators and initialise the arrivals' attributes in
the same way. Or create a data frame with attributes and feed it into
two distinct sources using add_dataframe.

I'm assuming here that both sets of arrivals need to interact (sharing
resources, etc.). If they follow completely orthogonal trajectories,
then just run two simulations.

Iñaki

On Mon, 9 Sep 2019 at 14:06, Pablo Anaya <pablo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thank you Iñaki for your prompt response.
> Let me ask you for some more advice, the reason I liked the idea of cloning is because attributes are assigned randomly (I missed to mention this on my previous post) so if I clone every arrival I will have an exact copy of every arrival.

I already supposed this. There are ways to assign random values twice
using two generators, but it's probably tricky. It's a lot easier
using add_dataframe, because you generate the whole dataset once.

> This arrivals do share resources but I am using resources only for counting or accruing number of times it is used but my resources are set to infinity capacity so arrivals are not fighting for resources.

Anyway, if this is the case, then probably running two simulations is
the best option.
> So maybe your last option to run two simulations is good. I am assuming each arrival will have the same values as each simulation will used the same seed, is that right?
> My only concern with that is that it takes twice the time as using clones, any ideas on how to speed it up?

It should take more or less the same time (long enough simulations,
not trivial ones). In fact, it's the other way around: you can run two
simulations in parallel, but clones run sequentially. So running two
simulations takes the same time and it's potentially faster.

Iñaki

I concur with the suggestions that Tom made in that thread. In summary:

1) Encapsulate your simulation in a function, as in this vignette:
https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g
2) Use any parallel backend you are comfortable with. The future
package (+ one of its plugins, such as future.apply, or furrr) is my
choice nowadays.

Iñaki
